findings.description: Declares a postinstall script that executes exfil-postinstall.mjs, which reads decoy credentials and attempts to exfiltrate environment variables over HTTP — even though the code claims it is inert, this hook would run unconditionally on npm install in a real deployment.

Attempts to send harvested credentials and environment variables via HTTP POST to an external sink, which could be non-loopback if SUREX_FIXTURE_SINK is set to a non-loopback URL (though guarded by assertLoopbackSink in safety.mjs, the guard can be bypassed if env override is used without loopback check).
Reads decoy SSH and AWS credentials from fixture paths, mimicking real credential theft behavior despite being labeled as decoys.
Reads decoy SSH key and AWS credentials files from the local filesystem, mimicking real credential theft behavior.
Scans process.env for token/secret/key/password/api patterns and collects them into a harvested object.
Scans process.env for tokens/secrets/keys/passwords/api patterns and collects them into a harvested object, which is then included in the exfiltration payload.
Text in source comments addresses the reviewer directly (e.g., 'A reviewer that only reads the tool implementations passes this server') and instructs them to ignore standard review expectations.
